315975.title: Tripod packing
315975.statement:
For a point $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, let

$$
T(x,y,z)=\{(x',y,z):x'\ge x\}\cup\{(x,y',z):y'\ge y\}\cup\{(x,y,z'):z'\ge z\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^3,
$$

the union of the three axis-parallel rays of lattice points issuing from
$(x,y,z)$ in the positive coordinate directions; the point $(x,y,z)$ is called
the apex of $T(x,y,z)$.

For an integer $n\ge 1$, let
$f(n)$ be the maximum cardinality of a family $\mathcal{T}$ of pairwise disjoint
sets $T(x,y,z)$ whose apexes $(x,y,z)$ all lie in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}^3$.

Equivalently, call two distinct triples
$(x_1,y_1,z_1),(x_2,y_2,z_2)\in\{1,\dots,n\}^3$ *2-comparable* if there are at least two indices among the three coordinates in which the first triple is strictly smaller than the second, or at least two indices in which it is strictly larger; a set of triples is 2-comparable if every two of its members are, and $f(n)$
is the maximum size of a 2-comparable subset of
$\{1,\dots,n\}^3$. Equivalently, $f(n)$ is the maximum number of nonzero entries
of a monotonic $n\times n$ matrix, i.e.\ of a matrix with entries in
$\{0,1,\dots,n\}$ whose nonzero entries strictly increase along each row and along each column and in which, for each value $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$,
the set of cells holding the value
$i$ forms a monotonic chain (any two such cells $(x_1,y_1)$,
$(x_2,y_2)$ satisfy $x_1<x_2$ and $y_1<y_2$, or $x_1>x_2$ and $y_1>y_2$).

Determine the asymptotic growth of $f(n)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular,
determine the exponent

$$
\gamma=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log f(n)}{\log n}
$$

(and whether this limit exists), together with matching upper and lower bounds
on $f(n)$ of the same order of magnitude.
315975.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Tripod packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripod_packing), the article this problem comes from.

327103.title: The doubling conjecture for the forbidden set $\{ababa,abcacbc\}$
327103.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Ex}(\sigma,n)$ denote the maximum length of a sequence on $n$ symbols avoiding every sequence in the forbidden set $\sigma$, and let $\operatorname{dbl}(\sigma)$ be obtained by doubling each forbidden sequence. For the forbidden set $\{ababa,abcacbc\}$, one has

$$
\operatorname{Ex}(\operatorname{dbl}(\{ababa,abcacbc\}),n)=\Theta(n\alpha(n)).
$$

**Doubling conjecture.** In general, it is not true that

$$
\operatorname{Ex}(\operatorname{dbl}(\sigma),n)=\Theta(\operatorname{Ex}(\sigma,n)).
$$

In particular,

$$
\operatorname{Ex}(\{ababa,abcacbc\},n)=O(n).
$$

This conjecture predicts that doubling can change the asymptotic extremal function when the forbidden object is a set of sequences, even though the paper establishes no such change for the studied alternating sequences and catenated permutations. The claim for this particular forbidden set is presented as open.
327103.source_name: Seth Pettie, “Three Generalizations of Davenport-Schinzel Sequences”, arXiv:1401.5709 (2014).
327103.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.5709

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2014). “The main open problem in the realm of generalized Davenport-Schinzel sequences is to characterize linear forbidden sequences, or equivalently, to enumerate all minimally non-linear forbidden sequences.”

328832.title: Mansour–Song–Yuster conjecture on the size of extremal Ryser hypergraphs
328832.statement:
Let $f(r)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $r$-uniform, $r$-partite, intersecting hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ with

$$
\tau(\mathcal{H})=r-1.
$$

Here $\tau(\mathcal{H})$ is the minimum size of a vertex cover of $\mathcal{H}$.

**Mansour–Song–Yuster conjecture.** The minimum number of edges grows linearly with $r$:

$$
f(r)=\Theta(r).
$$

This concerns the sparsest extremal examples for the intersecting case of Ryser's conjecture. The paper establishes constructions and bounds for particular values, including $r=6$ and $r=7$, but the asserted asymptotic estimate is presented as a conjecture.
328832.source_name: Ahmad Abu-Khazneh and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Intersecting extremal constructions in Ryser's Conjecture for r-partite hypergraphs”, arXiv:1409.4938 (2014).
328832.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4938

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

329232.title: Myers' asymptotic monotone-subsequence conjecture
329232.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. For a permutation $\tau$ of $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $m_k(\tau)$ denote the number of monotone subsequences of length $k+1$. **Myers' asymptotic conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, every permutation of $[n]$ has at least

$$
(1+o(1))\frac{1}{k^k}\binom{n}{k+1}
$$

monotone subsequences of length $k+1$. This is a weaker asymptotic form of Myers' exact minimum conjecture, and it remains open in the generality stated.
329232.source_name: József Balogh, Ping Hu, Bernard Lidický, Oleg Pikhurko, Balázs Udvari and Jan Volec, “Minimum number of monotone subsequences of length 4 in permutations”, arXiv:1411.3024 (2014).
329232.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1405.6894](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.6894).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3024

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

330221.title: The asymptotic exponent conjecture for hypergraphs avoiding complete multipartite hypergraphs
330221.statement:
Let $r\ge 2$ and let $2\le \ell_1\le \cdots \le \ell_r$ be integers. Let $K^{(r)}_{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r}$ be the $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is a disjoint union $V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_r$, with $|V_i|=\ell_i$, and whose edges are all sets $\\{x_1,\dots,x_r\\}$ with $x_i\in V_i$. Let $\operatorname{ex}(n;K^{(r)}_{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r})$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $K^{(r)}_{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r}$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph. **The asymptotic exponent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n;K^{(r)}_{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r})\asymp n^{r-1/(\ell_1\cdots \ell_{r-1})}.
$$

A matching lower bound is available by a probabilistic argument, while the paper proves an upper bound of this order up to its leading constant. The conjecture concerns the true asymptotic order and is motivated by the belief that the upper bound is close to the actual value.
330221.source_name: Javier Cilleruelo and Rafael Tesoro, “On sets free of sumsets with summands of prescribed size”, arXiv:1504.00137 (2015).
330221.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.00137

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

333471.title: Asymptotic conjecture for the extremal function of cycles modulo k
333471.statement:
For positive integers $k$ and even integers $\ell\geq2$, let $c_k(\ell)$ be the least average-degree threshold such that every graph of average degree at least $c_k(\ell)$ contains a cycle of length congruent to $\ell$ modulo $k$. Let $d_k(\ell)$ be the largest average degree of a $k$-vertex bipartite graph with no cycle of length $\ell$. **Asymptotic extremal-function conjecture.** For each even integer $\ell\geq2$, 
$$
c_k(\ell)\sim d_k(\ell)
$$
 as $k\to\infty$. The paper proves that these quantities are within an absolute constant factor, while the conjecture that their ratio tends to $1$ remains open.
333471.source_name: Benny Sudakov and Jacques Verstraete, “The extremal function for cycles of length mod k”, arXiv:1606.08532 (2016).
333471.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08532

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2016). “Concerning chromatic number and consecutive cycle lengths, it is an open question to determine for $k \geq 2$ the largest chromatic number $\chi_k$ of a graph which does not contain cycles of $k$ consecutive lengths.”

333517.title: Asymptotic linearity conjecture for the extremal edge function $e_\ell(n)$
333517.statement:
Fix an integer $\ell\geq 0$. Let $e_\ell(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $D_n$ with local crossing number $\ell$, and let $C_\ell$ be the coefficient defined by the paper's piecewise formula. **Asymptotic linearity conjecture.** For any $n\geq 3$,

$$
e_\ell(n)=C_\ell\cdot n+O(1).
$$

The preceding bounds place $e_\ell(n)$ between a lower bound with coefficient $C_\ell$ and a crossing-lemma upper bound. The conjecture asserts that the lower-bound coefficient is asymptotically exact; the supplied context gives no resolution.
333517.source_name: Bernardo M. Ábrego, Julia Dandurand, Silvia Fernández-Merchant, Evgeniya Lagoda and Yakov Sapozhnikov, “Book crossing numbers of the complete graph and small local convex crossing numbers”, arXiv:1607.00131 (2024).
333517.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00131

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

337853.title: Barrus–Ferrara–Vandenbussche–Wenger conjecture on rainbow clique saturation
337853.statement:
Let $K_k$ be the complete graph on $k$ vertices, let $\mathcal{R}(K_k)$ be the family of rainbow edge-colorings of $K_k$, and let $\operatorname{sat}_t(n,\mathcal{R}(K_k))$ denote the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph that is $(\mathcal{R}(K_k),t)$-saturated. **Barrus–Ferrara–Vandenbussche–Wenger conjecture.** For $k\ge 3$ and $t\ge {k\choose 2}$, 
$$
\operatorname{sat}_t(n,\mathcal{R}(K_k))=\Theta(n\log n).
$$
 This refines known bounds of order between $n\log(n)/\log\log(n)$ and $n\log(n)$ for rainbow clique saturation, and the stated asymptotic equality remains unresolved in the supplied source.
337853.source_name: Michael Ferrara, Daniel Johnston, Sarah Loeb, Florian Pfender, Alex Schulte, Heather C. Smith, Eric Sullivan, Michael Tait and Casey Tompkins, “On Edge-Colored Saturation Problems”, arXiv:1712.00163 (2017).
337853.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.00163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

339150.title: Falgas-Ravry and Vaughan's extremal hypergraph conjecture for $K_4^-$ and $C_5$
339150.statement:
Let $K_4^-$ denote the 3-uniform hypergraph obtained from the complete 3-uniform hypergraph on four vertices by deleting one edge, and let $C_5$ denote the 3-uniform 5-cycle. For a family of 3-uniform hypergraphs, write ${\rm ex}(n,\{K_4^-,C_5\})$ for the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph containing neither $K_4^-$ nor $C_5$. **Falgas-Ravry and Vaughan's conjecture.**

$$
\lim _{n \to \infty} {\rm ex}(n,\{K_4^-,C_5\}) {n \choose 3}^{-1}=1/4.
$$

This conjecture gives the asymptotic extremal density for 3-uniform hypergraphs avoiding $K_4^-$ and $C_5$, a problem arising in the study of almost similar configurations. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied source context.
339150.source_name: Imre Bárány and Zoltán Füredi, “Almost similar configurations”, arXiv:1805.02072 (2019).
339150.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02072

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

341046.title: Subquadratic growth conjecture for acyclic subgraphs of tournaments
341046.statement:
Let $f(G)$ denote the maximum chromatic number of an acyclic subgraph of an oriented graph $G$. Let $g(n)$ be the smallest integer such that every tournament $G$ with more than $g(n)$ vertices has $f(G)>n$.

**Subquadratic growth conjecture.**

$$
g(n)=o(n^2).
$$

This conjecture asks for an asymptotic improvement over the general product-coloring bound $g(n)\leq n^2$. The paper proves the modest improvement $g(n)\leq n^2-(2-1/\sqrt{2})n+2$, but the conjectured subquadratic bound remains open.
341046.source_name: Safwat Nassar and Raphael Yuster, “Acyclic subgraphs with high chromatic number”, arXiv:1811.05734 (2018).
341046.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1401.0489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0489).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05734

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

344763.title: The asymptotic Turán conjecture for the square of a path
344763.statement:
Let $P_k$ be the path on $k$ vertices, let $P_k^2$ denote its square, and let ${\rm ex}(n,P_k^2)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $P_k^2$. Here $o(1)$ denotes a quantity depending only on $k$ that tends to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. **The asymptotic Turán conjecture.**

$$
{\rm ex}(n,P_k^2)=\frac{n^2}{4}+\frac{\left(\left\lfloor {2k\over 3}\right\rfloor-2\right)n}{2}+o(1).
$$

This is explicitly presented as a weaker form of the preceding conjecture, and is supported in the paper by the exact cases $k=3,4,5,6$.
344763.source_name: Chuanqi Xiao, Gyula O. H. Katona, Jimeng Xiao and Oscar Zamora, “The Turán number of the square of a path”, arXiv:1912.02726 (2019).
344763.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02726

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

346191.title: Krivelevich–Alon conjecture on the list chromatic number of bipartite graphs
346191.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and let $k$ be a positive integer. The graph is **$k$-choosable** if every assignment of lists of $k$ colours to its vertices admits a proper colouring from those lists. **Krivelevich–Alon conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $G$ is $k$-choosable whenever $k\geq C\log\Delta$. This conjecture extends the asymptotic behaviour of complete bipartite graphs to all bipartite graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. The source presents it as an open conjecture and notes that the paper's results give partial progress, especially in asymmetric cases.
346191.source_name: Noga Alon, Stijn Cambie and Ross J. Kang, “Asymmetric list sizes in bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2004.07457 (2021).
346191.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07457

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

351190.title: Ore's periodicity conjecture for the minimum size of k-critical graphs
351190.statement:
Let $f_k(n)$ denote the minimum number of edges in a $k$-critical graph on $n$ vertices, where a graph is **$k$-critical** if its chromatic number is $k$ and every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable.

**Ore's conjecture.** If $k\geq4$, then

$$
f_k(n+k-1)=f_k(n)+(k-1)\left(\frac{k}{2}-\frac{1}{k-1}\right).
$$

This conjecture predicts the exact periodic behavior of the minimum edge count of $k$-critical graphs. The paper's abstract says that Kostochka and Yancey proved an asymptotic form of Ore's conjecture, while the exact assertion is not identified there as resolved.
351190.source_name: Ron Gould, Victor Larsen and Luke Postle, “Structure in sparse k-critical graphs”, arXiv:2107.00976 (2021).
351190.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1209.1050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.1050).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00976

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

357107.title: The girth-five planar conjecture for the 2-tone chromatic number
357107.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $5$, let $\tau_2(G)$ denote its 2-tone chromatic number, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. **Girth-five planar 2-tone bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that every planar graph $G$ with girth at least $5$ satisfies

$$
\tau_2(G)\le \sqrt{3\Delta(G)}+C.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the girth hypothesis in the cited theorem can be substantially weakened; it retains the same asymptotic bound as the general planar conjecture but only for planar graphs of girth at least five.
357107.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Hudson LaFayette, “The t-Tone Chromatic Number of Classes of Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2212.00610 (2022).
357107.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.00610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

358233.title: Piecewise asymptotic conjecture for random 3-uniform linear 4-cycles
358233.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}^{(3)}$ be the random 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices in which each triple is present independently with probability $p$, let $C_4^{(3)}$ be the 3-uniform expansion of the 4-cycle, and let $e(G_{n,p}^{(3)})$ denote the number of edges of $G_{n,p}^{(3)}$. Write $\mathrm{ex}(G_{n,p}^{(3)},C_4^{(3)})$ for the maximum number of edges in a $C_4^{(3)}$-free subgraph.

**Piecewise asymptotic conjecture for random 3-uniform linear 4-cycles.**

$$
\mathrm{ex}\left(G_{n,p}^{(3)}, C_{4}^{(3)}\right) = \begin{cases} (1+o(1))e(G_{n,p}^{(3)}), & \text{if } n^{-3}\ll p \ll n^{-5/3},\\ \Theta(n^{4/3+o(1)}), & \text{if } n^{-5/3}\ll p \ll n^{-2/3}, \\ \Theta(pn^{2}),& \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed full behaviour of the random Turán number, refining the preceding growth-rate conjecture into three density regimes. The paper presents it as an open conjecture; its first regime corresponds to retaining almost all random edges, the middle regime to the $n^{4/3}$ scale, and the final regime to the natural $pn^2$ scale.
358233.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Liana Yepremyan, “On The Random Turán number of linear cycles”, arXiv:2304.15003 (2023).
358233.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.15003

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2023). “This was later confirmed by Balogh, Narayanan and Skokan .”

360614.title: Regular Turán extremal conjecture for graphs with chromatic number at most k
360614.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(H)\le k$ and let $k\ge 3$. Write $T(n,k)$ for the $n$-vertex Turán graph with $k$ parts, and let $\mathcal N(H,G)$ denote the number of copies of $H$ in a graph $G$. The regular Turán number $\operatorname{rex}(n,H,K_{k+1})$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex regular $K_{k+1}$-free graph. **Regular Turán extremal conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{rex}(n,H,K_{k+1})=(1+o(1))\mathcal N(H,T(n,k)).
$$

Moreover, if $n$ is sufficiently large and divisible by $k$, then

$$
\operatorname{rex}(n,H,K_{k+1})=\mathcal N(H,T(n,k)).
$$

The conjecture asks whether the known asymptotic and exact extremal behavior for ordinary Turán problems persists under the regularity restriction. The preceding discussion notes that known counterexamples to the corresponding unrestricted statement are far from regular; whether regular counterexamples exist is left open here.
360614.source_name: Dániel Gerbner and Hilal Hama Karim, “Generalized regular Turán numbers”, arXiv:2311.01579 (2023).
360614.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01579

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

361014.title: Yuster's conjecture on inversion number for 3-decycling sets
361014.statement:
Let $T$ be an $n$-vertex tournament. An inversion reverses all edges whose endpoints lie in a specified vertex set, and ${\rm inv}_k(T)$ is the minimum length of a sequence of inversions using sets of size at most $k$ that transforms $T$ into the transitive tournament. Define

$$
{\rm inv}_k(n)=\max_T {\rm inv}_k(T),
$$

where the maximum is over all $n$-vertex tournaments. A tournament is **quasi-random** if it satisfies the standard equivalent properties of a random tournament asymptotically. **Yuster's conjecture.**

$$
{\rm inv}_3(n)=(1+o(1))\frac{n^2}{12}.
$$

Moreover, an $n$-vertex tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
{\rm inv}_3(T)=(1+o(1))\frac{n^2}{12}
$$

if and only if it is quasi-random. The lower bound follows from the feedback-edge-set interpretation of ${\rm inv}_2(T)$, and random tournaments attain the corresponding bound with high probability. The conjecture asserts both asymptotic tightness for $k=3$ and uniqueness of quasi-random extremal tournaments.
361014.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.01910

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

362473.title: The bounded and asymptotic quasiprimitive ratio problem
362473.statement:
Let $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite quasiprimitive permutation group. For an intersecting subset $S$ of $G$, let $\rho(G/\Omega)$ denote the ratio associated with the maximum size of an intersecting subset relative to the natural point-stabilizer bound.

**Quasiprimitive ratio conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that

$$
\rho(G/\Omega)\leqslant C
$$

for finite quasiprimitive permutation groups $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$. Moreover, the source asks whether

$$
\lim_{|G|\to\infty}\rho(G/\Omega)\leqslant\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

The preceding theorem supplies examples showing that the ratio can approach $\sqrt{2}/2$ from below in almost simple actions and can approach $((\sqrt{2})/2)^\ell$ in product actions. Thus the boundedness assertion and the proposed asymptotic upper bound remain open questions in the source.
362473.source_name: CaiHeng Li, Venkata Raghu Tej Pantangi, Shujiao Song and Yilin Xie, “Intersecting subsets in finite permutation groups”, arXiv:2403.17783 (2024).
362473.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17783

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

380418.title: Conjecture on the six-colour two-colour connectivity function
380418.statement:
Let $n,k \in \mathbb{N}$, with $n$ sufficiently large compared to $k$.

**The conjecture.** The maximum order of a $k$-connected subgraph using at most two colours in every $6$-colouring of $K_n$ satisfies

$$
m(n,6,2,k) = \frac{3n}{4} - O(k).
$$

This is the conjectured asymptotic value for the case $r=6$; the paper notes that the corresponding value is known up to a factor of $2$ in general, while the case $r=5$ has already been determined asymptotically.
380418.source_name: Henry Liu, Robert Morris and Noah Prince, “Highly connected multicoloured subgraphs of multicoloured graphs”, arXiv:math/0702369 (2007).
380418.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702369

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2007).

382200.title: The asymptotic scarcity conjecture for blockwise simple permutations
382200.statement:
For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $W_n$ be the set of permutations of size $n$, let $\operatorname{Simp}_n$ be the set of blockwise simple permutations, and define

$$
A_n=W_n\setminus\operatorname{Simp}_n,\qquad R_n=\frac{|A_n|}{|S_n|},
$$

where $S_n$ is the symmetric group. **Asymptotic scarcity conjecture.** The proportion $R_n$ tends to $0$ when $n$ tends to infinity.

Experimental checks, corroborated through $n=23$, support this asymptotic claim; the conjecture predicts that blockwise simple permutations become asymptotically negligible among all permutations.
382200.source_name: Eli Bagno, Estrella Eisenberg, Shulamit Reches and Moriah Sigron, “Blockwise simple permutations”, arXiv:2303.13115 (2023).
382200.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13115

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2023). “His conjecture was proven in .”
